institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The spoken language in the host country, the reputation of the school I was about to attend, the culture, my connection to the place and whether or not I could see myself live and thrive in this country/city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was accessible, but it would have been nice to be guided more by International Education in Copenhagen. They did not really reach out to help us.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive much assistance, but since I signed up for a Welcome Programme, we had a team leader who was there to help us, and I actually found this quite helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not very easy, very hard in fact.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It takes a long time to find, and it is expensive. And you might need to compromise a lot in terms of living standards. In general, start looking very early. It is not to your advantage that you are not French. They dont speak a lot of english, and they don't appreciate foreigners.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was some online registration beforehand, and then we just needed to pick up a student card. Overall it was easy enough for me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are many offices to reach out to, and they are fast to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that you have a very little window of time to register for courses, so prepare yourself thouroughly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I study on the third year, but the courses were for second year students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Differs a lot. In Copenhagen the teaching is much better structured, and you always know exactly what is expected from you.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Politics, Identity and Belonging in a Changing World, Introduction to International Politics and Foreign Policy Analysis, European Integration and its Challenges and Decision-making Process of the European Union (An insider's view)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Comparative Politics, even though it is a lot of work. Also Introduction to International Politics and Foreign Policy Analysis.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Medical bills since I got sick during the stay, public transportation (I got a fee twice), food is insanely expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive, and housing as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot to choose from, litteraly anything you can think of, they probably have a team for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't attend any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy Paris nightlife, the many cozy restaurants and bars, the clubs that are very exclusive, and of course all of the free museums are a must. I also recommend going to watch some games, for example Basketball or football.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough for me, France is not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be shy. Go to some bars, speak to people in class, but most importantly LEARN FRENCH. Also you can go on apps such as Bumble, where you can find friends to meet up with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier, for sure. But also, the general attitude towards foreigners. French people, especially adults are not always that friendly towards you if you dont speak their language. But even if you do, they wont always be too welcoming.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The parisians know how to enjoy life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: E-mail your proffessor if you are sick, and therefore wont be able to attend class. They might not mark you as absent. Learn some french. And dont be scared by the many requirements for the classes, prioritize to live life to the fullest in Paris and drink some wine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Learn french.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and living in Paris in general.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier and finding housing. But also the stress from fearing to get sick and be marked as absent, since Sciences Po only allows you to have two absences.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
